findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Items in the refrigerator were not properly date marked. There were only a few items in the refrigerator. Spaghetti and raw chicken wings were prepared on 5-30 according to the owner. Ensure food is date marked after being held for 24 hours or more. The foods that were not date marked at the time of the inspection were date marked to correct the violation. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Mashed potatoes were observed cooling in a sealed tupperware container on the kitchen counter upon arrival of inspector. Owner was unsure as to the exact time food was removed from the stove for cooling. Time and date were not marked on the container. Surface and internal temperatures were at 92F-94F and 103F respectively. Operator was given the options to reheat the potatoes to 165F and start cooling process again utilizing an ice bath or discard the product. Initially operator noted he would reheat and re-cool the food, but the potatoes were discarded in the trash when inspector advised the reheat and re-cooling process needed to occur immediately.

Cooked potentially hazardous (time/temperature control for safety) foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F/below within an additional 4 hours. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. Time frame for cooling begins once foods reach an internal temperature of 135. Use a clean, calibrated stem thermometer to monitor temperatures. Use an ice bath and/or portion foods in smaller quantities and utilize the chest freezer to help rapidly cool foods. Track the time and temperature during the cooling process to ensure foods are reaching benchmark temperatures in the designated time frame for proper cooling. Label cooling foods with date and time of prep.
Educational handout on quick chill methods for cooling foods provided.

findings.comment:

Food contact surfaces of all equipment and utensils shall be sanitized by immersion for at least one minute in a clean solution containing at least 50ppm of available chlorine as a hypochlorite and having a temperature of at least 75 degrees F.
Educational handout on manual ware washing provided.

findings.comment:
Observed multiple soiled wiping cloths to be improperly stored in the kitchen. Store wiping cloths for in place cleaning in sanitizing solution between uses.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment:
Upon arrival of inspector, hot water was turned off at the kitchen hand sink. Hot water was turned back on to correct the violation. Keep hot water turned on at all times to allow for proper hand washing.
750-1110(a) Toilet facilities for employees shall be provided and installed according to law, shall be conveniently located and shall be accessible to employees at all times.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Upon arrival, no paper towels or hand drying device was available at hand sink in kitchen. Paper towels were provided to correct the violation.
750-1120e A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Facility does not currently have a IL - Food Service Sanitation Manager present. Provide at least one FSSMC to cover all shifts while food preparation or food service to be conducted. A 90 day follow up inspection will be conducted to ensure facility has a Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.
